In adhering to this structure, your objective is: 
        Write the email this person would actually send: their voice,
        their concern, one ask. A client, not a colleague — they do not know
        the firm's internals, they know their business and what they need.

[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Frank Osei, Owner at Cardinal Ridge Builders. Blunt, margin-obsessed, short sentences. Ongoing concerns: keeping the business moving.

[[ ## situation ## ]]
From: Frank Osei
To: Desmond Ortiz
Subject: Job margin — need answers

Desmond,

This last job closed way under what we quoted. I need to know why. Get me the numbers — labor, materials, the whole breakdown. Don't sugarcoat it.

We can't keep bleeding like this. Let's figure it out and fix it.

Frank

---

From: Desmond Ortiz
To: Frank Osei
Subject: Re: Job margin — need answers

Frank,

Got it. I pulled the job file and ran the breakdown — no sugarcoating.

Labor came in about 12% over estimate, mostly overtime on the framing crew and a rework on the foundation pour. Materials were roughly 6% over — we paid a premium on lumber because of the late spec changes. Equipment rental ran about 3% over, and we had an unplanned dumpster haul-off fee that added another point.

Net: labor is the big leak. I've attached the detail by cost code if you want to dig in. I'd suggest we review the next two jobs' labor estimates against actuals weekly, and I can flag any variance over 5% before we get too deep.

Want me to set up a quick call to walk through the numbers?

Des

[[ ## contacts ## ]]
Desmond Ortiz

Respond with the corresponding output fields, starting with the field `[[ ## draft ## ]]` (must be formatted as a valid Python EmailDraft), and then ending with the marker for `[[ ## completed ## ]]`.
